newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Highveld Steel says strike to hit H2 profit.
newsitem.headline: Highveld Steel says strike to hit H2 profit.

text.p: South African group Highveld Steel and Vanadium Corp Ltd said on Wednesday that a strike at its iron and steelworks would see its second half profit come in lower than the first half.
The firm said in a statement that it had initially forecast a similar profit for both periods, but the strike had changed that.
"It is unlikely that this forecast will be met despite the fact that there is a full order book with a heavy export load," the firm said.
The firm called the strike by members of the National Union of Metalworkers of South Africa (Numsa) "illegal, unnecessary and damaging".
Highveld said it was not yet able to determine the full cost of the strike and the exact extent of the negative impact on the second half results.
"However, production at the works has resumed smoothly," it said.
The workers downed tools after a black artisan assistant was allegedly assaulted by a white supervisor.
Numsa has said the artisan was given the same punishment as the supervisor after an internal disciplinary hearing. Both men were given a final written warning valid for six months.
Highveld slammed Numsa for not taking the dispute before the Industrial Council or requesting arbitration before declaring a strike.
"Regardless of the merits of the assault case, the whole essence of neogiatated agreements is that they bind the parties to use the agreed procedures," the firm said.
The strike, whiuch began, on October 22, ended on November 4 when Numsa accepted arbitration.
